Devon Park: Heads-up — saw a 18–22% drop in tokens/sec for eu-west between 02:10–02:30 UTC last night, no infra alerts, but tail latencies spiked. Posting quick dump.
Devon Park: ```
region=eu-west window=02:05..02:35
avg_tokens_per_sec=18.2k (prev baseline 22.4k)
concurrent_reqs_peak=1.9k
observed_slab_evictions=37
kv_cache_misses=+42%
```
Nguyen Tran: Oof. Any tenant skewing the GPU slabs?
Devon Park: Looks like 3 tenants did short ~30s big-batch bursts that triggered slab reassign and preemption. When slab shares changed, warmup + KV rehydrate caused throughput to tank for adjacent tenants.
Maria Lopez: Can you share the slab allocation timeline? curious about allocation churn frequency.
Devon Park: ```
00:10:55 assign slab-A -> tenant: alpha (50->100GB)
00:11:23 preempt slab-B -> tenant: beta (100->40GB)
00:12:05 reclaim slab-A -> alpha finished
...repeat x3 within 15m
```
Sam B.: So eviction noise + KV cold-start = wasted tokens and concurrency headroom drop. Ballpark how much extra GPU-hours did this cause?
Devon Park: Estimate ~2.4 GPU-hours during that 20m window due to inefficient priming and smaller effective batching. Cost hit ~ $120 (on reserved math) but more importantly SLO risk.
Nguyen Tran: We should model this as two signals: instantaneous demand (burstiness) and slab-share inertia (how fast we move allocations). If inertia is too low, churn costs > capacity savings.
Jules: Agreed. Proposal: introduce a short-term smoothing policy — a leaky-share buffer that enforces min-share floor + damped adjustments. Rough heuristic: 5min half-life on share rebalance, min_share=3%, no preempt during cold-cache warmup window (90s).
Maria Lopez: Sounds reasonable. Any numbers on tokens/sec improvement in sim?
Devon Park: Ran a quick sim with historical bursts for eu-west:
- baseline (immediate reassign): median tokens/sec -19% during burst tail
- smoothing (5min half-life): median tokens/sec -6%
- cost delta: smoothing +0.9 GPU-hours but SLO regained.
Nguyen Tran: Can we express this as concurrency->tokens mapping so product understands? Example: 1k concurrent @avg_len=32 -> ~32k tokens/sec. If slab churn reduces effective concurrency by 25%, tokens/sec drops accordingly.
Sam B.: Would like to see an A/B plan: stage the smoothing on a subset of racks for 48h, monitor tokens/sec, kv-miss, and tail-p99.
Devon Park: I'll draft the canary config. Key knobs: half_life_secs=300, min_share_pct=3, warmup_protect_secs=90.
ops-bot: deploybot: canary rollout triggered by Devon Park for cluster eu-west-canary (config: smoothing-v1)
Nguyen Tran: Also add instrumentation: per-tenant slab-change-rate metric + cumulative kv-miss-by-tenant so we can correlate.
Jules: +1 on instrumentation. If sim numbers hold, run for 48h and then decide to flip default.
Maria Lopez: FYI node-affinity difference in eu-west racks might amplify this — add a rack_label dimension to the sim.
Devon Park: noted. I'll run rack-aware sims and post results in this thread tomorrow morning. Thanks all :raised_hands:
